title: The last look
hookLine: he lifts the curtain and smiles to see the people praying in rows (Bukhari)

lines: WATCHING IT GO ON WITHOUT YOU.
cards: Have you ever watched something you built carry on without you? A parent in the doorway at a child's wedding, watching the room fill. A teacher glancing back into a classroom where the students are working on their own.

It was a Monday, early, the dawn prayer. Abu Bakr was at the front of the mosque, and behind him the people stood in their lines. Next door, in Aisha's room, a hand reached for the curtain that hung in the doorway.

teach.b: The companion Anas ibn Malik was in those rows, and Sahih al-Bukhari keeps his memory of it. The Prophet ﷺ lifted the curtain of the room and stood looking at them as they prayed in their rows.

He smiled, Anas says, then laughed with happiness. Anas says his face looked like a page of the Qur'an, bright. The people saw him and nearly broke off their prayer for sheer joy, thinking he was coming out to them.
Abu Bakr started to step back to make room.
The Prophet signaled with his hand: complete your prayer. Then he went back inside and let the curtain fall. He died later that same day.
Consider what was in front of him. In the early years in Mecca, a handful of people had prayed in secret, some of them beaten for their faith.

teach.h: FROM A SECRET FEW TO FULL ROWS.
teach.b: Now there were rows, straight and full, shoulder to shoulder behind a leader who was not him.

The rows, sufuf in Arabic, mattered to him. The hadith say he used to straighten them himself, telling people: straighten your rows. The last thing he saw of his community wasn't a victory or a crowd cheering him.
It was people praying together, without needing him in front. Anas doesn't say why he smiled. He only says what he saw: the rows, carrying on.

how: Muslims pray in straight, close rows behind one imam, and before congregational prayer the imam often reminds people to straighten their rows, as the Prophet did.

games.q: you're praying in the rows at dawn, and the curtain of Aisha's room lifts. the people nearly break their prayer for joy. what does the Prophet ﷺ do?
o: come out and take the front.
signal: complete your prayer, then let the curtain fall.
games.why: he signaled them to finish, went back inside and let the curtain fall. he died later that day.

practice: Picture a place full of people going about their day: a train, a supermarket, a playground, a mosque, your own kitchen at breakfast.
Nobody is looking at you; let yourself smile at them gently, the way you'd look at something you love carrying on. If you pray, you can pray for them without their knowing.

wordCard.voice: Sufuf. The rows of worshippers standing together in prayer — the last sight the Prophet smiled at on his final morning. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: rows, the lines of people standing together in prayer. singular saff.

carryVoice: Your line: he smiled at the rows. Some joy is watching it go on without you. Day two hundred eighty-nine, done.

sources.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 680; Sahih Muslim 419 (Anas: he lifted the curtain, smiled at the rows, signaled them to complete the prayer, and died that day)
